A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REAL framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original KI-VQA and conflict-discrimination experiments, component ablations, latency measurements, and supplementary experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds conflict-discrimination evaluations, guidance and perturbation ablations, robustness tests, and error attribution.

M1.justification: REAL-VQA construction, RPA-SFT, and RPGD retain the same procedures, components, and Algorithm 1. Section 3.3 adds conceptual distinctions without specifying an operational change to the method.

E1.justification: Appendix C.1 and Table 13 add conflict-discrimination evaluation on e-SNLI-VE with native contradiction labels and manually annotated InfoSeek-human. This materially broadens coverage to different conflict sources, beyond the retained REAL-VQA, E-VQA, ScienceQA, and MMKC evaluations.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparators and Greedy/VCD/CAD comparisons remain. New diagnostic comparisons introduce uniform and random guidance, blank-image and Gaussian-blur alternatives, and oracle pivot signals in Tables 6, 8, and 15. Changed Prophet citations do not establish a changed evaluated method.

E3.justification: New experiments specify uniform token intervention, replacement of 50% of detected pivots, alternative visual perturbations, and two oracle controls. Existing splits, metrics, model sizes, retrieval settings, and training budgets remain unchanged; the additions are targeted evaluation variants.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component removals and decoding comparisons, v2 tests whether accurate detection signals drive gains, compares visual perturbation choices, examines imperfect versus oracle pivots, and decomposes errors into retrieval, extraction, mitigation, and visual-language reasoning failures (Tables 6, 8, 15–16). These substantially expand the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental seed counts, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests. The ten stochastic GPT-4o quality scores used during dataset construction were already documented in v1 and remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark scores are unchanged, but substantial results are added. Table 13 reports Qwen3-VL-8B zero-shot/RPA-SFT F1 of 71.6/80.5 on e-SNLI-VE and 63.4/75.0 on InfoSeek-human. Table 15 newly reports E-VQA accuracy of 39.3 under 50% pivot corruption versus 41.4 with predicted pivots. Tables 6, 8, and 16 add guidance, perturbation, and error-source results.

T1.justification: The reasoning-pivot definitions, conflict criterion, and decoding equations remain unchanged. Section 3.3 provides qualitative distinctions rather than new formal reasoning; Appendix C.3's oracle experiments do not introduce a mathematical proof or derived bound.

C1.justification: The four central contributions and claims of generalizable conflict detection and improved KI-VQA remain. Although the abstract replaces 'state-of-the-art' with 'superior,' the introduction still explicitly claims SOTA performance, and the conclusion retains the same scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of guidance precision and visual perturbation, interprets natural-conflict results as evidence against synthetic-artifact overfitting, and attributes robustness to intact visual evidence. Appendix C.3 asserts negligible error accumulation, while C.4 identifies intrinsic visual-language reasoning as a remaining bottleneck and advances causal interpretations. The original limitations paragraph is retained.

D1.justification: Dataset-construction details in Appendix A, implementation and hyperparameters in Appendix B, and prompt templates in Appendix D are unchanged after matching relocated content. No new code/data access information or implementation specifications accompany the added evaluation controls.

R1.justification: Section 3.3 adds explicit positioning against global graph indexing and sequential question decomposition. The references add e-SNLI-VE and replace the introductory LLaVA++ citation with DeepSeek-V3. These are limited changes within the retained research framing.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 3.3, Appendix C.3–C.4, localized explanatory paragraphs, acknowledgements, and expanded affiliation/publication text. The main narrative order, method exposition, and most appendix prose remain intact rather than undergoing extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: New Tables 6, 8, 13, 15, and 16 display the additional experiments. Existing tables, Algorithm 1, and figures are repositioned as text flows, and Figure 8 adjusts failure-case image crops. The established table formats, figure content, and overall layout remain largely stable.

improvement.justification: The added guidance, perturbation, natural-conflict, and error analyses provide useful evidence beyond v1's existing ablations. The net improvement is limited by missing sampling/adaptation details for the new datasets and an unspecified error-attribution procedure. Table 15 also leaves its differing base scores unexplained relative to Table 5, and one corruption condition does not justify the broad claim that error accumulation is 'fundamentally negligible.'
